cohorts.summary: Reviewers encounter crashes, missing auto-saves, and pathfinding bugs, while highlighting management mechanics.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks an auto-save feature, which can result in lost progress when crashes occur.

citations.review_text: it bugs out too much, and i cant save my progress
game crashed and didnt auto save wasted my time I should have saved but im really angrt

A lot of little bugs and glitches throughout the game.
if I re-entered the game screen without turning off fullscreen, the mouse in-game ended up misaligned, which I could only fix by leaving and re-entering fullscreen mode. A lot of the times, tribe or nest members struggle to pathfind to their destinations, which requires you to manually unstuck them. Pressing escape to skip the cutscene sometimes crashed the game, and the game doesn't have any auto saves, mind you. Worst of all, I was doing a pacifist run and I got to the tribal stage on hard difficulty, and I was unable to progress due to a bug which made allying with other tribes impossible. 

The space stage is like a separate game from the rest. Instead of following the same neat kind of progression, this part suddenly requires you to invest much more into the game. And personally, it's pretty boring.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe pathfinding and AI issues during the creature and tribal stages, requiring manual intervention to unstick tribe or nest members.

citations.review_text:
Wow, what a brilliant concept. A game where you choose how you evolve from the earliest stages of life to a space farer probably would've had me obsessed as a kid, and I really regret having never played it while I was younger. You basically get to make your own vaguely dinosaur-like creature, so that would've been good enough for me. The problem is that I'm a loser adult that hates fun now, and unfortunately Spore's execution did not bring its winning idea to life for me.

Don't get me wrong, the level of customisation is more than satisfactory and there's definitely some charm to growing out and interacting with different species, but a lot of what this game offers in terms of gameplay just feels underwhelming even if it isn't necessarily bad. I could feel this the most during the creature stage, where you're given the most individual control of all stages and yet the only thing to do is to walk around and decide whether you want to eradicate the species you run into or not. Combat largely boils down to spamming buttons with varying cooldowns and watching health values drop, with clunky AI and pathfinding, and social rituals are action-matching contests that are almost purely decided by stat numbers.

It might improve as you go through the stages, and admittedly I did find the tribal stage to be the most immediately intriguing due to some actual management and strategy features, but it still wasn't that fun and with the help of another issue that I'll get to, I never saw it through. Maybe it'd be presumptuous to say that it feels as though they didn't have enough funding when making the game, this could very well have been their vision and that it's meant to be palatable to children, but I also can't lie and pretend that I don't think the developers wanted to do more when initially conceptualising something like Spore, nor does the lack of interesting mechanics being intentional make it any easier to enjoy interacting with.

citations.review_text:
First thing: This game is incredibly good (except tribal stage) and I can confidently say I had fun playing every single part of this game (except tribal stage), And I would totally advise you buying and playing this game!

Second thing: You should NOT buy this game off of steam, The steam version doesn't have access to the online features which are a big portion of the game so for your own sanity buy this off of something else, I recommend you look up which versions of spore actually work.

I have accumulated potentially several thousands of hours of Spore through different launchers, DLCs, and modded clients. I spent (or wasted?) much of my adolescence on this game for no reason because I yearn to create amalgamations and imperialism that life and reality could not even muster up. I have since then stopped probably, but I leave this review now:

yeah its pretty good ig try it if you want

Steam sometimes (aka 99% of the time) won't let you connect unless you play through the EA client or whatever. just purchase carefully on here, or get it wisely on the dinky EA launcher. also the game sometimes has these crash bugs but its honestly really avoidable or just bearable to some extent.
